Alternative.description:
One rejected option: the negative space every executor re-proposes
when nobody told it the option was closed.

cites.description: The identifiers the rejection rests on.
cites.title: Cites

option.description: The option that was on the table.
option.title: Option

Alternative.title: Alternative

Amendment.description:
One amendment: its number and date, the typed diff (empty for an
execution finding that changed nothing typed), and the words.

changes.description: The typed diff; empty for an execution finding that changed nothing typed.
changes.title: Changes

title.description: What the amendment did, in a line.
title.title: Title

Amendment.title: Amendment

Budget.description: What an attempt may spend (S-0001/domain); None on an axis is no bound there.

iterations.description: The most attempts the loop makes before it escalates; a drafting run's drafts.
iterations.title: Iterations

tokens.description: The tokens the broker lets an attempt spend, enforced mid-run (S-0045/D-4).
tokens.title: Tokens

wallclock_minutes.description: The wall-clock bound of an attempt, in minutes — declared, read by no leg yet.
wallclock_minutes.title: Wallclock Minutes

Budget.title: Budget

Change.description:
One typed edit an amendment made (S-0053/D-4): the prior value is read at
amendment time, which is the only moment it exists.

before.description: The prior value, read at amendment time.
before.title: Before

Change.title: Change

Decision.description:
One decision row, whole (S-0056/D-2): grade, text and paths — the three
fields a contract copies at mint — with its consequence, rationale,
citations, check and the stamp the tool last wrote on it.

check.description: A command whose exit code judges the row; authored, never derived (S-0053/D-15).
check.title: Check

check_state.description: The check's gate state, promoted per row by amendment (S-0054/D-4).
check_state.title: Check State

check_twin.description: The test that proves the check can fail (S-0054/D-4).
check_twin.title: Check Twin

cites.description: The identifiers this row builds on.
cites.title: Cites

consequence.description: What follows from the decision — the reason handed to the executor beside the rule.
consequence.title: Consequence

fingerprint.description:
`<content>/<rule>` as `stamp` writes it, empty until the tool has changed
the row once; `fingerprint_drift` reads it (S-0053/D-5).
fingerprint.title: Fingerprint

id.description: `D-n` inside its own document, `S-NNNN/D-n` in memory (S-0058/D-1).
id.title: Id

paths.description: The area the row governs; a LOCKED row must declare one.
paths.title: Paths

rationale.description: Why the row was decided this way; never copied onto a contract.
rationale.title: Rationale

superseded_by.description: The row that replaced this one, once it is retired.
superseded_by.title: Superseded By

text.description: The decision itself — the sentence a contract copies at mint.
text.title: Text

Decision.title: Decision

DesignSection.description:
One prose section: the key a log cites and a markdown body the
engine never parses (S-0053/D-3, S-0056/D-3). The heading is the key and the
number is the position (S-0057/D-2); order is the list's.

key.description: The key a log cites, `S-NNNN/<key>`; the heading is derived from it.
key.title: Key

md.description: The markdown body the engine never parses.
md.title: Md

DesignSection.title: DesignSection

GradedRow.description:
One inherited row as a landing keeps it (S-0059/D-10): the identifier
and the grade the contract carried, which is what the `Torve-Decisions`
trailer used to say and what outlives the task directory.

grade.description: The grade the contract inherited at mint.
grade.title: Grade

id.description: The row's identifier, `S-NNNN/D-n`; local inside its own document.
id.title: Id

GradedRow.title: GradedRow

InheritedDecision.description:
One row as a contract carries it (charter §3; S-0054 S-0054/D-1): grade,
text and paths copied at mint and fingerprinted; `consequence` beside
them so the executor gets the reason, and `check` — a command whose
exit code judges the row — which the runner appends to the battery as
a `decision:<id>` gate at `check_state`, with `check_twin` the test
that proves the check can fail (S-0054/D-4). A contract minted before
S-0054 loads with the four defaults, which is the old behaviour.

check.description: A command whose exit code judges the row, run as the `decision:<id>` gate (S-0054/D-4).
check.title: Check

check_state.description: The check's gate state: `shadow` until an amendment promotes it (S-0054/D-4).
check_state.title: Check State

check_twin.description: The test that proves the check can fail (S-0054/D-4).
check_twin.title: Check Twin

consequence.description: Why the row exists — the reason beside the rule, so the executor gets both (S-0054/D-1).
consequence.title: Consequence

grade.description: The row's grade as it stood at mint — copied, so the executor reads what the author settled.
grade.title: Grade

paths.description: The area the row governs, declared; what enables the silence check.
paths.title: Paths

text.description: The decision's text as it stood at mint.
text.title: Text

InheritedDecision.title: InheritedDecision

Invariant.description:
A statement with the paths it holds over and the command that proves
it.

check.description: The command that proves it; exit 0 is holding.
check.title: Check

id.description: `I-n` inside its own document, `S-NNNN/I-n` in memory.
id.title: Id

statement.description: What must hold, over the paths.
statement.title: Statement

Invariant.title: Invariant

Landing.description:
What one task found, kept beside the rows it informs (S-0057/D-7): the
task, its phase and attempt, the commit when the lander knew it (the
runner's rides in the candidate commit whose trailers name the task,
so it leaves the field empty), when, by whom, and the log's entries.

agent.description: Who landed it — the agent identity the runner composes, or a session.
agent.title: Agent

base.description: The commit the attempt built on, from the log's pin (S-0058/D-12).
base.title: Base

commit.description: The commit the work landed in, when the lander knew it (S-0058/D-12).
commit.title: Commit

decisions.description: The rows the contract carried, with their grades (S-0059/D-10).
decisions.title: Decisions

entries.description: The task log's entries, kept here beside the rows they cite (S-0057/D-7).
entries.title: Entries

phase.description: The phase its contract was minted from; 0 when none was.
phase.title: Phase

Landing.title: Landing

LogEntry.description:
One divergence entry as the task log carries it and a landing keeps
it (S-0057/D-7): the row it cites, what reality said, the evidence, what
the executor did. `class` is the log's key; the field is `entry_class`
because the word is Python's.

action.description: What the executor did: halted, departed or decided.
action.title: Action

at.description: The instant the entry was written (S-0058/D-7).
at.title: At

class.description: `class` in the log: discovery, spec-gap, drift or irreducible.
class.title: Class

decision.description: The row the entry cites, `S-NNNN/D-n`; local inside the row's own document.
decision.title: Decision

evidence.description: A `path:line` citation or a backticked command with its output (S-0005/D-4).
evidence.title: Evidence

grade.description: The row's grade as the executor read it, or UNLISTED when no document lists it.
grade.title: Grade

kind.description: What happened: contradicted, departed, resolved or blocked.
kind.title: Kind

notes.description: Anything else the reader of the log should know.
notes.title: Notes

proposal.description: The row the executor proposes for the author to append.
proposal.title: Proposal

LogEntry.title: LogEntry

Phase.description:
One mintable unit of the phasing: what `torve plan` derives a
contract from.

acceptance.description: The acceptance commands the contract gets; exit 0 is satisfied.
acceptance.title: Acceptance

character.description: The phase's structural or routine character, copied onto its contracts (S-0034/D-1).
character.title: Character

depends_on.description: The phases that must land first.
depends_on.title: Depends On

intent.description: One paragraph: what changes and why — never steps (S-0001/D-7).
intent.title: Intent

phase.description: The phase number; the tasks of one phase are disjoint and may run in parallel.
phase.title: Phase

scope.description: The allow globs the contract gets; a LOCKED row's paths must fit inside them.
scope.title: Scope

tier_variant.description: The seat variant the contract routes to, when one is named (S-0027/D-3).
tier_variant.title: Tier Variant

Phase.title: Phase

Question.description: One entry of a `yaml questions` fence.

id.description: `Q-n` inside its own document, `S-NNNN/Q-n` in memory.
id.title: Id

settled_by.description: The amendment or row that settled it.
settled_by.title: Settled By

Question.title: Question

Scope.description:
allow/deny globs, gitwildmatch semantics. deny wins over allow; an empty
allow means unconstrained (S-0002/scope-in-detail).

allow.description: Globs of what the task may touch, gitwildmatch; empty means unconstrained.
allow.title: Allow

deny.description: Globs the task may not touch; deny wins over allow.
deny.title: Deny

Scope.title: Scope

Task.description:
The task contract, `.torve/tasks/T-NNNN/contract.yaml` (S-0001/domain, §6).

`decisions` has no default on purpose: an empty list is legal but must be
explicit (S-0007/D-5), so `decisions-reported` can distinguish "none apply"
from "the field was forgotten".

character.description:
The phase's declared structural or routine character, copied verbatim from
the phasing entry at mint (S-0034/D-1). Absent by default — a task with no
character routes on the seat alone, same as one with no tier_variant.
character.title: Character

decisions.description:
The rows inherited at mint, grade and paths copied (S-0007/D-5); an empty
list is legal but must be explicit.
decisions.title: Decisions

depends_on.description: The tasks that must land before this one dispatches.
depends_on.title: Depends On

intent.description:
One paragraph: what changes and why — never steps (S-0001/D-7, S-0001/A-4).
Optional until the S-0001/A-4 execution makes minting enforce it; contracts
minted before the amendment carry none.
intent.title: Intent

parent.description:
Set only at adoption of a decomposition's children (S-0026/D-5): projections
group by it; dispatch, lane and store never read it — ordering stays
depends_on alone.
parent.title: Parent

phase.description: The phasing entry the contract was minted from; 0 when no phase minted it.
phase.title: Phase

role.description: What the run does: implement, review (S-0005/D-9), revert (S-0010) or draft (S-0020).
role.title: Role

schema_version.description: The contract's shape version: 2 names the document as `spec` (S-0059/D-1).
schema_version.title: Schema Version

scope.description: What the attempt may and may not touch (S-0002/scope-in-detail).

source.description:
What asked for the work (S-0060/D-3): a source identifier, `S-NNNN` or
`<kind>/<slug>`, never parsed for inheritance. `spec` says whose rows this
contract inherits and this says why it exists; a contract may carry both,
either or neither, and the record reads this before `spec` before
`operator`.
source.title: Source

spec.description:
The document the contract was minted from, by identifier and never by path
(S-0059/D-1) — `document_dir` is the one lookup that finds it. None is the
document-less lane: an operator's ask, a standing job.
spec.title: Spec

targets.description:
The tasks a review examines (S-0005/the-review-contract, S-0005/D-9) or the
tasks and shas a revert undoes (S-0010/revert-as-a-role): the contract shape
is parameterised by role, no new mechanism. Only those two roles carry targets.
targets.title: Targets

tier.description: The seat that runs it — planner, executor or reviewer (S-0004).
tier.title: Tier

tier_variant.description:
An optional dotted variant under the seat (S-0027/D-3), resolved as
`tier.variant` in the tiers mapping — a variant refines a seat, never invents
one, and role semantics still key on `tier` alone. Naming a variant that is
not configured is a refused dispatch, not a fallback.
tier_variant.title: Tier Variant

title.description:
A short human name (S-0007/A-1): the landing subject and every board row read
it; empty falls back to the intent's first line. The planner mints it from the
phase title; a drafter may set it.
title.title: Title

Task.title: Task

after.description:
The documents whose landed tree this one's work builds on, as document ids
— never phases (S-0085/D-1, S-0085/D-5); `depends_on` keeps its one meaning,
decision inheritance, and says nothing about trees.
after.title: After

contract_example.description: One contract as the planner would mint it, for the reader.

phasing.description: The mintable units `torve plan` derives contracts from.
phasing.title: Phasing
